input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. 20.1 gives an express Vendor duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates against third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables. 20.2 extends the Vendor indemnity to Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct and fraud. 20.4 supplies the standard procedure (prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of the defence, with a materiality-of-prejudice qualifier and a settlement-consent protection favouring the indemnified Party). Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is properly narrow, covering only unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. 20.5 additionally provides the fallback-level procure/modify/replace remedies with a refund of prepaid and implementation Fees (straight-line three-year basis) and bars termination of unaffected Services. The fallback super-cap of 3x annual fees is unnecessary and would be adverse to us: under 21.3 indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims and therefore uncapped. The permissive fallback exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) are absent from 20.1, which is more favourable to us. No redline proposed.
